newsitem.title: UK: Lengthening unsold Brent queue keeps N.Sea depressed.
newsitem.headline: Lengthening unsold Brent queue keeps N.Sea depressed.

text.p: A queue of unsold late March and early April Brent cargoes, growing longer by the day, kept North Sea crude markets under pressure on Friday, traders said.

Three Brents, due to load April 5-9, were turning wet on Friday, adding to the seven loading in the first six days of the month and already in the hands of BP. Some traders said two late March Brent cargoes were also still available.
"Nobody's been offering (Brent) today but if you look at the CFDs, it's clear the market is weaker again," said a trader.
Next week's dates shed five cents to trade at May Brent -51 cents.
May gained four cents to $20.22 a barrel by 1317 GMT.
Intermonth paper spreads also lost ground, April May trading at +7 cents, five or six cents weaker than on Thursday.
May/June also fell back to trade at +10 cents.
Shipping brokers said Glencore provisionally fixed the ULCC Jahre Pollux to take 350,000 tonnes of Brent to the U.S. in late March or early April but traders doubted the arbitrage was open.
"You would have to swallow 15-20 cents a barrel to make Brent work into the U.S. Gulf at the moment," said one.
Other North Sea grades were better supported.
But BP's maintainance of run cuts at Rotterdam, where Texaco restored throughput on Thursday, could block further gains.
In the Mediterranean Russian Urals crude remained depressed with traders reporting little buying interest and stiff competition from other sours.

Small parcels of Russian Urals were getting picked off at values around dated Brent -$1.30/-$1.25 a tonne delivered, but several handy-size vessels were still looking for homes with refinery maintenance keeping demand to a minimum.
April prices fixings for Syrian and Algerian crudes were still unconfirmed.
